meaning: On this moonlit Margazhi morning, the girls call to one another to come bathe at dawn. The dark-hued lion-cub, son of Nandagopa — lotus-eyed Narayana himself, with a face like the radiant moon — will grant them the parai, the drum. Let them worship their Pavai goddess in a way the whole world sings about.
tamil: கார்மேனிச் செங்கண் கதிர் மதியம் போல் முகத்தான்
பாரோர் புகழப் படிந்து ஏல் ஓர் எம்பாவாய்.
title: மார்கழித் திங்கள்
translit: kaarmEnich chengaN kadhir madhiyam pOl mugaththaan

meaning: O people of the world, hear the vows we keep for our Pavai worship: we sing the holy feet of the Lord who sleeps softly on the ocean of milk. We will take no ghee, drink no milk, bathe before dawn each day, wear no kohl, tie no flowers in our hair, do no forbidden act, speak no ill of others — and we will give alms and charity as much as we can, lifting others out of sorrow.
tamil: உய்யுமாறு எண்ணி உகந்து ஏல் ஓர் எம்பாவாய்.
title: வையத்து வாழ்வீர்காள்

meaning: If we sing the name of the noble Lord who grew tall and measured the worlds, and bathe for our Pavai vow, then without harm the land will see three rains a month. Tall red paddy will rise, fish will dart through the fields, spotted bees will sleep drunk on honey inside the blue lotuses, generous great cows will fill pot after pot from their full udders — and unfailing wealth will fill the country.
tamil: வாங்கக் குடம் நிறைக்கும் வள்ளல் பெரும் பசுக்கள்
நீங்காத செல்வம் நிறைந்து ஏல் ஓர் எம்பாவாய்.
title: ஓங்கி உலகளந்த
translit: vaangak kudam niRaikkum vaLLal perum pasukkaL

meaning: O rain-god born of the ocean, hold nothing back! Plunge into the sea, drink your fill, soar up roaring. Darken like the body of the Primal Lord of the deluge, flash like the discus in Padmanabha's strong-shouldered hand, thunder standing like his right-turned conch, and rain down ceaselessly like arrows loosed from his Saranga bow — pour on this world that it may flourish, and we too will bathe joyfully in Margazhi.
tamil: ஊழி முதல்வன் உருவம் போல் மெய் கறுத்துப்
மார்கழி நீராட மகிழ்ந்து ஏல் ஓர் எம்பாவாய்.
title: ஆழிமழைக் கண்ணா
translit: oozhi mudhalvan uruvam pOl mey kaRuththup

meaning: To the wonder-worker, the prince of everlasting northern Mathura, who played on the banks of the pure deep Yamuna, the jewel-lamp arisen in the cowherd clan, Damodara who made his mother's womb blessed — we came in purity, showered pure flowers and bowed, sang with our mouths and pondered him in our hearts. Then the wrongs of the past, and those yet to come, will burn away like cotton cast in fire — so sing, O Pavai!
tamil: தூயோமாய் வந்து நாம் தூமலர் தூவித் தொழுது
தீயினில் தூசாகும் செப்பு ஏல் ஓர் எம்பாவாய்.
title: மாயனை
translit: thooyOmaay vandhu naam thoomalar thoovith thozhudhu

meaning: See, the birds are twittering — did you not hear the great sound of the white conch from the temple of Garuda's lord? Wake up, girl! Holding in your heart the Primal Seed who drank the ogress's poisoned milk, who kicked the deceitful cart-demon to pieces, who sleeps on the serpent of the deluge-waters — the sages and yogis softly rise chanting the great name of Hari. Let it enter your heart and cool it, O Pavai.
tamil: உள்ளம் புகுந்து குளிர்ந்து ஏல் ஓர் எம்பாவாய்.
title: புள்ளும் சிலம்பின காண்
